title: On the precise boundary of the Néel antiferromagnetic phase in the Shastry-Sutherland model
authors: Rongyi Lv, Xiangjian Qian, Mingpu Qin
abstract: The ground state phase diagram of the Shastry-Sutherland model remains controversial. In particular, the nature of the transition between the plaquette valence bond solid (PVBS) phase and the Néel antiferromagnetic (AFM) phase is still under debate. While some studies suggest a direct transition between the two phases, others propose the existence of a narrow intermediate quantum spin liquid regime. To address this issue, we perform large-scale Density Matrix Renormalization Group calculations to determine the Néel AFM phase boundary in the Shastry-Sutherland model. By applying staggered boundary pinning fields and directly measuring the bulk staggered magnetization, and through systematic extrapolations with respect to truncation error as well as careful finite-size scaling, we find that the staggered magnetization remains finite across the controversial region $0.78 \lesssim J_{1}/J_{2} \leq 0.81$, which was suggested to host a quantum spin liquid phase in some studies. Together with the previously established consensus placing the PVBS phase boundary at $J_{1}/J_{2} \approx 0.78$, these results provide evidence against the existence of an intermediate quantum spin liquid phase and support a direct PVBS--Néel AFM transition in the Shastry-Sutherland model.
summary: This theoretical study uses advanced DMRG techniques to map the phase diagram of the Shastry-Sutherland model. By precisely measuring the staggered magnetization across a debated region, the authors argue against the existence of an intermediate quantum spin liquid phase. Their findings strongly support a direct quantum phase transition between the PVBS and Néel AFM states.
main_problem: The paper aims to precisely determine the phase boundary separating the plaquette valence bond solid (PVBS) phase from the Néel antiferromagnetic (AFM) phase in the Shastry-Sutherland model.
main_result: The calculations show that the staggered magnetization remains finite across the controversial region $0.78 \lesssim J_1/J_2 \leq 0.81$, providing evidence for a direct PVBS--Néel AFM transition and ruling out an intermediate quantum spin liquid phase.
method: Large-scale Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations were employed, utilizing staggered boundary pinning fields and systematic finite-size scaling to extrapolate results to the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Shastry-Sutherland model, which is believed to describe the physics of $	ext{SrCu}_2(	ext{BO}_3)_2$. The Hamiltonian involves nearest-neighbor ($J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) couplings.
key_observables: Staggered magnetization ($m_s$), ground state energy density ($e$), and sublattice staggered magnetizations ($m_A^s, m_B^s$).
important_parameters: The ratio of couplings $J_1/J_2$, particularly around the critical region $0.78 \lesssim J_1/J_2 \lesssim 0.82$, and the pinning field strength ($h_{	ext{pin}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extrapolating physical quantities using finite-size scaling with respect to the DMRG truncation error ($\epsilon$) and system size ($L_y$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup using pinning fields and show finite-size scaling results for both the ground state energy density and the staggered magnetization across various coupling ratios.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies DMRG to calculate observables like staggered magnetization and energy density, performing rigorous finite-size and truncation-error extrapolations to pinpoint the phase boundary between the PVBS and Néel AFM regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides high-precision numerical evidence regarding the nature of quantum phase transitions in frustrated magnetic systems, which is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron physics in materials like cuprates.

The black and blue lines represent the J1 and J2 interactions, respectively. We set J2 = 1 throughout this work. A pinning field along the z direction with strength hpin is applied at the open boundaries (orange hatched regions). The staggered magnetization ms is measured on the two central columns (red dashed box). FIG. 3. Finite-size scaling of the ground state energy density e for the Shastry-Sutherland model at J1/J2 = 0.8. The bulk energies extrapolated to zero DMRG truncation error (see the Supplemental Materials [44] for details) for Ly = 6, 8, 10, and 12 with different aspect ratios α are shown. The upper and lower panels correspond to hpin = 0.2 and 0.5, respectively. The resulting thermodynamic limit estimate, e∞= −0.4490(1) (the purple star), is consistent with the previous iPEPS result [27, 45].

Finite-size scaling of the staggered magnetization ms extrapolated to zero DMRG truncation error (see the Supplemental Materials [44] for details) for different coupling ratios: (a) J1/J2 = 0.78, (b) 0.79, and (c) 0.81.
